Cymbra Lingua · beta

Your vocabulary, where you already read

A browser extension that highlights the Spanish words you do not know yet, right on the page. No app to open, no revision session to schedule: you read, you learn.

ChromeFirefox (desktop)Safari (iPhone, iPad, Mac)

Available on Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers, on Firefox (desktop) and on Safari (iPhone, iPad, Mac). Made for English speakers learning Spanish. Also for French speakers learning English or Spanish: the interface and the translations are in French. Also for Spanish speakers learning English: the interface and the translations are in Spanish.

🖍️ Highlighted in place

Unknown words appear highlighted on the page itself — without breaking the site you are reading.

📊 An honest percentage

The icon shows how much of the current page you actually know. One number per page, not an inflated score.

👆 One click to understand

Click a highlighted word: its dictionary form, its translation, its frequency in plain language, and three buttons — “I know it”, “+ Deck”, “Ignore”. In Spanish, the card also names the tense and the gender.

🗂️ Deck and review

Captured words and phrases become cards, carrying the sentence you met them in. Review them from the side panel.

📴 Offline by construction

The analysis runs inside your browser, against a bundled dictionary. No page you read is ever sent anywhere.

📈 Your level, on the CEFR scale

An estimate of your vocabulary, anchored to A1→C2 rather than to a homemade badge. For Spanish, the levels are estimated from word frequency, as no CEFR list can be shipped freely.

🪪 Optional account

Signed out, everything stays local. Signed in to Cymbra ID, your deck and word statuses follow you across devices.

🧭 Spanish → English · English and Spanish → French · English → Spanish

Choose your languages in Settings: each page is read in its own.

What the dictionary covers

The share of the commonest words that have a gloss in the reader's language, measured the same way for each pair, in the dictionaries the extension ships.

Commonest words5,00010,00020,000
Spanish → English93%87%77%
English → French95%90%79%
Spanish → French88%77%64%
English → Spanish93%85%72%

Glosses come from Wiktionary and from translations written by people, never from machine translation. Extended translation, optional, serves Spanish to English, English to French, Spanish to French (through English) and English to Spanish.

What about music?

Lingua shares its account, its philosophy and its respect for your data with Cymbra Music, available on the App Store and Google Play.
